title: VPC residency policy enforcement + automated evidence/reporting for private deployments
creator: Lena Park
description: Implement end-to-end residency controls and automated compliance evidence for Private/VPC and on-prem deployments. Goals: 1) Allow customers to declare an explicit residency policy (allowed regions and sites) at the tenant level. 2) Enforce policy in the routing and failover layer to prevent automatic failover to disallowed regions for residency-sensitive workloads. 3) Expose retention settings (per-tenant and per-route TTLs) and ensure enforcement across private control plane and local agents. 4) Produce machine-readable evidence packages (audit log bundle + signed residency assertion) that operations and compliance teams can download on demand, and schedule periodic attestations. This ticket covers the enforcement plumbing, API surface, audit event schema, and the automated evidence generator for the Private control plane. UI and design polish are tracked in the attached PM/Design tasks.
acceptance_criteria: Tenant API accepts a residency policy JSON with allowed_regions, deny_fallback boolean, and retention_defaults
Serving router respects deny_fallback flag: requests marked residency-sensitive must not route to disallowed regions; explicit fallback routes allowed only if tenant sets override and approve audit
Control plane persists retention settings and emits structured audit events for policy changes and routing decisions

Automated evidence generator produces a downloadable ZIP with: residency-policy.json, routing-decision-log.ndjson (last 90 days), signed-assertion.txt (RSA2048 signature), and retention-ttl-report.csv
Evidence artifacts include stable timestamps and request hashes suitable for ingestion into customer GRC systems
End-to-end tests cover: policy creation, a blocked failover scenario, a permitted manual override flow, and retention TTL enforcement for expired cached artifacts
Documentation page (private residency) published and linked from console with example policies and CLI snippets
comments: 2025-02-10 - Kickoff: scoped by PM (Ava Chen). Initial design doc links added; blockers: legal wants explicit wording for 'residency' vs 'processing location'.

2025-02-14 - Architecture sync: proposed enforcement points: (1) edge router policy check, (2) control-plane admission gate, (3) local node agent guard. Diego volunteered to prototype router integration.

2025-02-20 - Prototype update: router prototype enforces allowed_regions for stateless requests; KV-cache affinity scenarios identified as edge case. Linked PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving/pull/2145
2025-02-25 - Legal: provided draft residency wording; requested audit trail of any manual overrides with approver and ticket link. Added requirement to evidence payload.
2025-02-27 - PM feedback: require scheduled attestations (monthly) and retain signed artifacts for 2 years by default unless tenant configures shorter retention.
2025-03-02 - Blocker: need dependency on ENG-7903 (secure key signing support in control plane). Working with infra to expedite.
2025-03-04 - Engineering: started work on audit event schema (ndjson lines) and evidence pack generator; added integration test harness for deny_fallback behavior.
migration_plan: Rolling migration: 1) soft launch - accept residency policies but default deny_fallback=false; collect telemetry for two weeks. 2) opt-in tenants can enable deny_fallback=true. 3) after validation window, default for new private tenants will be deny_fallback=false but provide migration tooling to evaluate blocked failovers.
rollback_plan: If enforcement causes regressions, flip router flag to 'policy-evaluate-only' to stop blocking decisions and continue collecting evidence. Evidence generator is read-only and safe to run anytime.
notes: Trade-offs: strict deny_fallback increases availability risk — mitigation via explicit multi-region allowed lists and per-route manual override with just-in-time audit. Chosen to favor compliance-first tenants while providing observability to measure availability impact. Retention defaults tuned to balance customer audit needs and storage cost.
